question: Should OpenClaw support static SecretRef values in `sandbox.docker.env`, knowing the resolved values become Docker container environment variables visible through Docker metadata?
rationale: This is a new security-sensitive config shape on an existing sandbox env surface; source review can prove the gap, but only maintainers can accept or reject the credential exposure boundary.

options.title: Accept linked PR path
options.body: Approve the static SecretRef-to-Docker-env behavior after confirming docs, audit/configure targets, and runtime resolution all preserve literal env compatibility.

options.title: Require non-env delivery
options.body: Keep this issue open for a different secret delivery design if Docker metadata exposure is unacceptable for SecretRef-backed values.

options.title: Reject the direction
options.body: Close this issue and the linked PR if OpenClaw should continue recommending custom images, mounted secret files, or other existing alternatives for sandbox credentials.

recommendation.title: Accept linked PR path
recommendation.body: Approve the static SecretRef-to-Docker-env behavior after confirming docs, audit/configure targets, and runtime resolution all preserve literal env compatibility.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history ties this account to both Docker env propagation and adjacent SecretRef runtime behavior.
